task:
Build "Nested and named support groups", step AC-1 of 6: support groups under groups and supporting statements, for The Discussion (plan id: nested-named-groups; acceptance criterion: AC-1; source requirements: docs/core-requirements.md; plan base commit 7644616031f5e30bed3392d7f876fcb400537d07). This task text is self-contained: everything needed to implement and verify this step is below.

## Goal

The plan's goal (verbatim):

Support groups can contain sub-groups, and a supporting statement can have its own support groups
as sub-arguments. Status propagates up the tree. Every new group has a required name, and a group's
name and type can be edited.

This task delivers only AC-1. A support group can be added under the thesis, under another support group or under a supporting statement, at any depth. Every other parent rule stays as it is.

Test design: `docs/test-plans/nested-named-groups-use-cases.md` (use cases UC-1 to UC-6 with flowcharts, clusters A to C with variables tables, open questions Q-1 to Q-4). The add-statement body is `AddStatementRequest(kind, parentId, text, groupType)`. `StatementResponse` carries the computed `stands` (supporting statements), `refuted` (counter arguments and rebuttals) and `holds` (non-empty groups only; empty groups have no `holds`), plus `editedAt` (always present, `null` until the first edit). Endpoints, all under `/api/v1/discussions`:
  - `POST /{id}/statements` adds a statement (201 with a `StatementResponse`).
  - `PATCH /{id}/statements/{statementId}` edits a statement (200). Before this plan it accepts only `text` and rejects `kind`, `parentId` and `groupType`.

  - `GET /{id}` returns the discussion with a flat list of statements in creation order, each with its `parentId`. Status is recomputed on every read and never stored.
- Errors: RFC 7807 `ValidationProblem` with status 400, and an `errors` object keyed by the camelCase field name (`parentId`, `name`, `groupType`, `text`, `kind`, `statementId`, `body`). An unknown discussion or statement returns 404 problem details.

## Acceptance criterion (verbatim from the plan)

- **AC-1** WHEN a client adds a support group, THE SYSTEM SHALL accept the thesis, another support
  group or a supporting statement as its parent, at any depth. A group may mix supporting
  statements and sub-groups. Supporting statements still attach only to groups, and counter
  arguments and illustrations still target only the thesis or a supporting statement. A wrong
  parent kind returns 400 naming `parentId`. Check: API integration tests for each newly allowed
  parent and each still-rejected one.

## Constraints (verbatim from the plan)

- Keep the API conventions (`/api/v1`, camelCase, GUIDs, RFC 7807). The only changes are the new
  `name` field on groups and the new allowed group parents.
- Counter arguments still cannot target groups, and illustrations still cannot be countered.
- No limit on nesting depth. The status engine and every recursive walk (outline rendering,
  cascade delete, serialization) must handle deep trees without recursion that could overflow.
- The schema change ships as an EF Core migration that preserves existing data, and the core and
  API projects stay storage-independent.
- No accounts or authorization; the endpoints are as open as the existing ones.

How they apply to this task: the only API change is the wider set of parents for `supportGroup`. There is no depth limit, and parent validation must not walk ancestors recursively. It needs only the parent's kind. No storage schema change is needed.

## Decisions that apply

- **D-1** Groups can nest inside groups and sit under supporting statements as sub-arguments. (Wayne)
- **D-4** No fixed nesting-depth limit. (Wayne)

## Implementation notes

- In `DiscussionRules.AllowedParentKinds`, change the `StatementKind.SupportGroup` row to `[Thesis, SupportGroup, SupportingStatement]`. Every other row stays exactly as it is:
  - `SupportingStatement` → `[SupportGroup]`;
  - `Illustration` and `CounterArgument` → `[Thesis, SupportingStatement]`;
  - `Rebuttal` → `[CounterArgument, Rebuttal]`.
- Check that `DiscussionService`, the endpoints and response mapping don't assume elsewhere that a group's parent is the thesis. The wrong-kind error still names `parentId`.
- Both storage providers must store and read back a group whose parent is a group or a supporting statement. `parentId` is already generic, so no schema change should be needed. If one turns out to be needed, stop and report it. Do not add a migration, because AC-3 owns the migration.

## Testing

Source: `docs/test-plans/nested-named-groups-use-cases.md`:
- UC-1: the main flow, alternate flows A1 to A4 and error flows E1 to E4, with the decision points "Parent kind is thesis, supportGroup or supportingStatement?", "Parent kind is supportGroup?", "Parent kind is thesis or supportingStatement?", "Parent kind is counterArgument or rebuttal?", "parentId present and a GUID?" and "Parent found in this discussion?";
- the Cluster A variables "Kind being added", "Parent kind", "`parentId` validity", "Nesting depth", "Alternation of group and support levels" and "Member mix of a group" (only the AC-1 part, that mixing is allowed);
- the store and read part of the Cluster C variable "Tree depth".

Leave out any test that needs status values for nested trees (AC-2), group names or `PATCH` of groups (AC-3), the UI (AC-4), or delete (AC-5).

The plan's check for AC-1 (verbatim): Check: API integration tests for each newly allowed
  parent and each still-rejected one.

xUnit unit tests (`tests/TheDiscussion.Core.Tests/DiscussionRulesTests.cs`):
- `AllowedParentKinds` and `CanAttach` for every addable kind against every parent kind (5 addable kinds × 6 parent kinds). Exactly the pairs listed above are allowed. A group has three allowed parents: `thesis` (unchanged), and `supportGroup` and `supportingStatement` (new).

API integration tests (`tests/TheDiscussion.Api.Tests`, `WebApplicationFactory` on the in-memory provider, for example a new `NestedGroupEndpointTests.cs`):
- Newly allowed parents. Each returns 201 with `kind: "supportGroup"`, the given `parentId` and `groupType`, `editedAt: null` and no `holds`, because the new group is empty. The next `GET` lists the group with that `parentId`. Cover:
  - a group under a top-level group (UC-1 A1);
  - a group under a nested group at depth 3;
  - a group under a supporting statement in a top-level group, which is a sub-argument (UC-1 A2);
  - a group under a supporting statement that sits in a nested group or in a sub-argument group (an alternating group → support → group chain);
  - a group under the thesis, which still works.
- Mixed members: a group that holds both supporting statements and sub-groups is accepted, and `GET` returns all of them with the right `parentId` (Cluster A "Member mix of a group").
- Rules that are unchanged, now exercised at depth (UC-1 A3 and A4). Each returns 201:
  - `supportingStatement` under a nested group and under a sub-argument group;
  - `counterArgument` and `illustration` under a nested supporting statement;
  - `rebuttal` under a counter argument on a nested supporting statement.
- Parents that are still rejected (UC-1 E3). Each returns 400 naming `parentId`, and nothing is stored (the next `GET` is unchanged):
  - `supportGroup` under an `illustration`, a `counterArgument` or a `rebuttal`;
  - `supportingStatement` under the thesis, under a supporting statement (top-level and nested), and under an illustration, a counter argument or a rebuttal;
  - `counterArgument` and `illustration` under a top-level group and under a nested group;
  - `rebuttal` under a group (top-level and nested) and under a supporting statement.
- `parentId` validity for `kind: "supportGroup"` (UC-1 E1 and E2; Cluster A "`parentId` validity"). Each of these returns 400 naming `parentId`, and nothing is stored: `parentId` missing, an empty string, not a GUID, a GUID that matches no statement, and the GUID of a statement in another discussion.
- An unknown discussion returns 404 (UC-1 E4).
- `kind: "thesis"` and an unknown kind still return 400 naming `kind` (Cluster A "Kind being added", boundary).
- A missing or invalid `groupType` on a nested group still returns 400 naming `groupType`. This is today's rule, now applied on the new parents.
- Depth (Cluster A "Nesting depth": boundaries 1, 2, 3, 1,000 and 1,001; "Alternation of group and support levels": a chain of 1,000 or more alternating levels):
  - A group is accepted at depth 1, 2 and 3.
  - A group is accepted under a parent at depth 1,000, so the new group sits at depth 1,001.
  - Repeat the depth case once with an alternating group → supporting statement → group chain of 1,000 or more levels.
  - Building the chain through the API is fine. For speed, you may instead seed it through the `IDiscussionStore` resolved from the factory's services and add only the last level through the API.
  - A `GET` of the deep discussion returns 200 with every statement, which shows serialization handles the deep tree.
  - A 10,000-level chain is an optional extra if it runs in reasonable time.

Storage contract tests (`tests/TheDiscussion.Storage.Tests/DiscussionStoreContract.cs`, run against in-memory and against PostgreSQL):
- A group stored under a group, and a group stored under a supporting statement, read back with the right `parentId`, `kind` and `groupType`, in creation order.
- A 1,000-level alternating chain is stored and read back complete on both providers. This is only the store and read part of Cluster C "Tree depth"; delete belongs to AC-5.

All existing tests must still pass, and their assertions must not change.
